The trip record gives an actual distance of 8.3 km against a recommended route of 6.7 km, a deviation of 1.60 km, which is more than the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, and the recorded events fix that excess to a bounded stretch of the trip: route_deviation_detected at 08:16:41 at Bishan Road / Braddell Road and route_rejoined at 08:26:16 at Thomson Road / Toa Payoh Rise, roughly 9m35s off the recommended route. The deviation distance is therefore establishable on the recorded distances, as POL-RD-22 requires, and is not within tolerance.

The driver-device trace independently shows which route was taken and when. Its map-matched road field puts the vehicle on Braddell Road from 08:16:32 and then on Toa Payoh Lorong 6 from 08:21:32 — the two roads the rider names, and neither of them on the recommended route, which runs Marymount Road. I use the trace only for which route was taken and when, as POL-RD-22 directs; I do not ask the judge to re-measure the deviation from the trace's 6.872 km, because POL-RD-22 says a sparse trace understates a route's length.

The reroute was not traffic-justified on the record. The LTA traffic record retrieved for the recommended route's Marymount Road segment, valid 07:39:02 to 09:09:02 and so squarely overlapping an 08:09-08:30 trip, reports advisory_type NONE, no incident, roadwork or closure on the segment, and speed bands 4-5 throughout; the derived justifies_reroute value is false. POL-RD-23 is explicit that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify a reroute, so the driver's explanation — 'Marymount Road every morning sure jam one' — cannot carry the reroute.

The driver never told the rider he was deviating. The chat log holds exactly two messages, both sent before the rider boarded (08:06:32 and 08:07:02, about where the car was parked), and the trip record's messages_during_trip is empty and its in_app_calls is empty, so nothing was sent or said at the 08:16:41 deviation point or at any time afterwards. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation; there is no recording in the record and the driver's own statement concedes the omission — 'Didn't think need to say.'

On POL-RD-24's matrix these facts sit in row (d): the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That is deviation_km 1.60 times per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, which is 1.15 SGD, with no surge applied to the excess distance fare and the figure rounded to the cent as POL-RD-24 provides. The same 1.15 SGD follows under row (b), because the driver did not inform the rider; the only row that would leave the charge standing is (a), which needs traffic justification AND a rider who was informed and agreed, and neither limb is met here.

There is no jurisdictional bar to the AI deciding this trip. POL-RD-25's additional 2 km limb is switched off in the loaded policy (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) and in any event the deviation is 1.60 km, under 2 km.

Nothing in the evidence package is impaired, so confidence is not capped below the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires. Every artifact I rely on — the trip record, the chat log, the fare breakdown and the LTA advisory — is graded COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired, and each of the deciding facts sits in at least one such artifact: the deviation in the trip record, the absence of notice in the chat log and trip record, the absence of traffic justification in the advisory, and the per-km rate in the fare ledger.

One limit on this claim, stated plainly so it is not overstated: the rider asks for 'about $3', but POL-RD-24 does not measure a route-deviation remedy by the fare difference the rider perceives. It fixes the remedy at the excess distance fare, and nothing in it licenses returning the whole trip fare — the surge multiple, the extra time fare and the gap between the rider's weekly expectation and today's metered total are not recoverable under this policy. The rider therefore asks the judge for the 1.15 SGD excess distance fare in full, not for the full contested sum.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: I have decided this on the platform's own records, and both sides' surviving claims point to the same figure.

The route and the deviation. The platform trip record (EV-TRIP-05001) gives an actual distance of 8.3 km against a recommended route of 6.7 km, a deviation of 1.60 km. POL-RD-22 (v2.1 1.3-1.4) measures the deviation from those recorded distances and uses the GPS trace only to show which route was taken, not to re-measure distance. The trace (EV-GPS-05001) confirms the vehicle left the recommended route at Bishan Road / Braddell Road (08:16:41) and rejoined at Thomson Road / Toa Payoh Rise (08:26:16), via Braddell Road and Toa Payoh Lorong 6 - the two roads the rider names and neither on the recommended Marymount Road line. The single deviation segment is 1.60 km, which exceeds POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The driver's own claims fixing the ceiling at 1.60 km are correct, and the rider's claim that the deviation is over tolerance is correct.

Traffic justification. The LTA traffic record for the recommended route's Marymount Road segment (EV-ADVIS-05001-01), valid 07:39:02 to 09:09:02 and so squarely covering the 08:09-08:30 trip, reports advisory type NONE - no incident, roadwork, closure or congestion - with speed bands 4-5 throughout. Under POL-RD-23 (v2.1 1.4), a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify a reroute. The driver's explanation that 'Marymount Road every morning sure jam one' therefore cannot carry the reroute, and his own account does not attempt to deny it.

Notice to the rider. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider by in-app chat, or verbally with a call recording, before or at the point of deviation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05001) holds only the two pre-boarding parking messages (08:06:32 and 08:07:02); messages_during_trip is empty and there are no call recordings. The driver's own statement concedes the omission - 'Didn't think need to say.' The rider's claim that no notice was given is correct.

The remedy. POL-RD-24's matrix gives exactly one row. The reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so row (d) applies: the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That is deviation 1.60 km times the per-km rate 0.72 SGD (EV-FARE-05001) = 1.152, rounded to 1.15 SGD, with no surge applied to the excess distance fare. Row (b), which the rider also invokes, does not apply because it requires the reroute to be traffic-justified, which it is not; the figure is the same in any event. The rider asked for 'about $3', but POL-RD-24 fixes the remedy at the excess distance fare and does not return the whole trip fare or the rider's perceived weekly fare difference - the rider's own claim correctly limits the request to 1.15 SGD, and the driver's claims correctly confine the refund to the deviation element. The fare ledger reconciles line by line to the 15.97 SGD charged (base 2.80 + distance 5.98 + time 3.78 + surge 2.51 + platform fee 0.90, tolls 0.00), so no fee, toll or surge line is chargeable back to the driver.

Confidence and jurisdiction. The deciding facts sit in artifacts graded COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, LTA advisory, fare breakdown), so the confidence cap is 1.0; nothing is impaired and no narration of an impaired artifact is required. The disputed value is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so an AI ruling is final at any confidence, and POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is comfortably met. POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in the loaded policy (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) and the deviation is 1.60 km in any event. No safety flag, human-only flag or fraud flag applies, so no escalation and no confidence uplift. No clause produces a referral: the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit, POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag and POL-NS-22 fee check all belong to no-show charges and are not engaged on a route deviation.

Outcome: 1.15 SGD of the trip's charge is returned to the rider; the rest of the charge stands.

Working through it in order: the deviation distance is measured, as POL-RD-22 (v2.1 1.4) directs, from the platform's own recorded distances — actual 8.3 km minus recommended 6.7 km = 1.60 km — and the GPS trace is used only to show which route was taken and when (the vehicle on Braddell Road and Toa Payoh Lorong 6 between the 08:16:41 departure and the 08:26:16 rejoin), not to re-measure distance. At 1.60 km the deviation exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance. On traffic justification, the LTA record for the recommended Marymount Road segment (valid 07:39–09:09, overlapping the 08:09–08:30 trip) reports type NONE with speed bands 4–5 and no incident, roadwork or closure; POL-RD-23 (v2.1 1.4) says a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify a reroute, so the driver's 'Marymount Road every morning sure jam one' cannot carry it. On notice, the chat log holds only two messages, both before the rider boarded (08:06:32, 08:07:02), and there are no in-app calls, so nothing was sent or said at the deviation point or after; POL-RD-21 (v2.1 1.1) requires notice by chat or on a call recording, and the driver's own statement concedes the omission ('Didn't think need to say'). These facts put the case in row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That figure is 1.60 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD, with no surge on the excess (POL-RD-24; v2.1 1.3). Both parties' core points are accepted: the rider is right that the route deviated, was not justified and was not notified, but the rider's request for 'about $3' exceeds what the policy provides — the remedy is the excess distance fare, not the whole fare difference or the total 15.97 SGD (base 2.80 + distance 5.98 + time 3.78 + surge 2.51 + platform fee 0.90), which reconciles line by line. The driver is right that recovery is capped at 1.15 SGD and that only the one recorded deviation segment is attributable. Every artifact relied on (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown, LTA advisory) is graded COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, so confidence is not capped below 1.0; the disputed value is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band at which an AI ruling is final at any confidence, no fraud flag is present, and the confidence meets the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires. POL-RD-25's extra 2 km limb is switched off in the loaded policy and the deviation is under it in any event. No clause produces a referral, and no monetary outcome runs to the driver.

ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances put this deviation over tolerance. The trip record gives an actual distance of 8.3 km against a recommended route of 6.7 km, a deviation of 1.60 km, which is more than the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, and the recorded events fix that excess to a bounded stretch of the trip: route_deviation_detected at 08:16:41 at Bishan Road / Braddell Road and route_rejoined at 08:26:16 at Thomson Road / Toa Payoh Rise, roughly 9m35s off the recommended route. The deviation distance is therefore establishable on the recorded distances, as POL-RD-22 requires, and is not within tolerance.

The driver-device trace independently shows which route was taken and when. Its map-matched road field puts the vehicle on Braddell Road from 08:16:32 and then on Toa Payoh Lorong 6 from 08:21:32 — the two roads the rider names, and neither of them on the recommended route, which runs Marymount Road. I use the trace only for which route was taken and when, as POL-RD-22 directs; I do not ask the judge to re-measure the deviation from the trace's 6.872 km, because POL-RD-22 says a sparse trace understates a route's length.

The reroute was not traffic-justified on the record. The LTA traffic record retrieved for the recommended route's Marymount Road segment, valid 07:39:02 to 09:09:02 and so squarely overlapping an 08:09-08:30 trip, reports advisory_type NONE, no incident, roadwork or closure on the segment, and speed bands 4-5 throughout; the derived justifies_reroute value is false. POL-RD-23 is explicit that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify a reroute, so the driver's explanation — 'Marymount Road every morning sure jam one' — cannot carry the reroute.

The driver never told the rider he was deviating. The chat log holds exactly two messages, both sent before the rider boarded (08:06:32 and 08:07:02, about where the car was parked), and the trip record's messages_during_trip is empty and its in_app_calls is empty, so nothing was sent or said at the 08:16:41 deviation point or at any time afterwards. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation; there is no recording in the record and the driver's own statement concedes the omission — 'Didn't think need to say.'

On POL-RD-24's matrix these facts sit in row (d): the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That is deviation_km 1.60 times per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, which is 1.15 SGD, with no surge applied to the excess distance fare and the figure rounded to the cent as POL-RD-24 provides. The same 1.15 SGD follows under row (b), because the driver did not inform the rider; the only row that would leave the charge standing is (a), which needs traffic justification AND a rider who was informed and agreed, and neither limb is met here.

There is no jurisdictional bar to the AI deciding this trip. The disputed value is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold at which an AI ruling is final at any confidence, and this record carries no fraud flag in either profile — driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0 — so the 0.95 uplift does not engage. POL-RD-25's additional 2 km limb is switched off in the loaded policy (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) and in any event the deviation is 1.60 km, under 2 km.

Nothing in the evidence package is impaired, so confidence is not capped below the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires. Every artifact I rely on — the trip record, the chat log, the fare breakdown and the LTA advisory — is graded COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired, and each of the deciding facts sits in at least one such artifact: the deviation in the trip record, the absence of notice in the chat log and trip record, the absence of traffic justification in the advisory, and the per-km rate in the fare ledger.

One limit on this claim, stated plainly so it is not overstated: the rider asks for 'about $3', but POL-RD-24 does not measure a route-deviation remedy by the fare difference the rider perceives. It fixes the remedy at the excess distance fare, and nothing in it licenses returning the whole trip fare — the surge multiple, the extra time fare and the gap between the rider's weekly expectation and today's metered total are not recoverable under this policy. The rider therefore asks the judge for the 1.15 SGD excess distance fare in full, not for the full contested sum.

On this record the most the rider can recover is the excess distance fare, and POL-RD-24 fixes that as the deviation distance times the per-km rate with no surge applied: 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.15 SGD. The rider's request for 'about $3' has no basis in the ledger, so the driver's exposure on this claim is 1.15 SGD and it cannot be stretched to the contested 3.00 SGD.

The deviation is measured only from the platform's recorded distances - 8.3 km actual minus 6.7 km recommended = 1.60 km - and POL-RD-22 expressly forbids re-measuring it from the GPS trace, so the excess cannot be argued upward from the rider's impression that the fare was 'clearly more'. The 1.60 km figure is the ceiling, whichever way the arithmetic is run.

There is only one departure from the recommended route on this trip: the trace shows the vehicle leave at Bishan Road / Braddell Road and rejoin at Thomson Road / Toa Payoh Rise, with no further departure before the drop-off. Nothing beyond the single recorded deviation segment can be attributed to the driver, so the excess cannot exceed the 1.60 km already counted.

The fare ledger reconciles line by line to the 15.97 SGD charged (base 2.80 + distance 5.98 + time 3.78 + surge 2.51 + platform fee 0.90, tolls 0.00), so there is no unexplained overcharge in the trip beyond the deviation element; under POL-RD-24 the refund is confined to the excess distance fare and no toll, fee or surge line is chargeable back to the driver.
